source: derived from newly authored cross-form curriculum, no lyrics or private archive fragments

cards.cue: R&B: let understated everyday actions carry intimacy. Use singable vowel-led hook contours, relaxed syncopated phrases and an earned hook variation; do not force technical density.
Cypher: preserve distinguishable performers, hand off rhyme pockets as answers and allow rest-space between parts. A shared refrain is optional; don't erase performer identities.
Lullaby: choose gentle repeatable imagery, shorter singable sentences and steady soothing movement. Do not manufacture complex internal rhymes or claim exact 6/8 timing without audio.
Uneven meter: plan stress and rest around a counted motif, then vary it consciously. Text is only an intended phrasing map, never proof of BPM or actual bar alignment.
Spoken word: let breath, meaning and purposeful silence determine line breaks. End rhyme and pop chorus labels are not mandatory; make a concrete perspective shift.
Funk: write compact rhythm-first calls and short replies, with room for bass and drum fills. Give recurrence a communal function rather than filling verses with repeated slogans.
High-speed rap: pack distinct internal assonance pockets into intelligible verbs and events; pivot sound families and punctuate with short stress-gate lines. Avoid syllable salads.
Folk ballad: privilege a clear narrative voice, physical details and consequential turns. Use a recurring couplet only when its meaning can evolve; do not equate folk with generic rural imagery.
